patterns: what is the structure of a kundiman
is kundiman a filipino love song
entries.answer: The kundiman is a love song of Filipino origin, and it is significant beyond being traditional because its structure is built for two voices: the first line is sung by one person, the second is the response, and the song is therefore a conversation rather than a statement. That form reflects its origin, since it was adapted from Spanish and Mexican forms that came to the Philippines through the colonial period, and the words are usually Tagalog while the melodic shape and harmonic accompaniment are largely from those older traditions. It is normally sung a cappella or with a small ensemble, since the vocal line carries the argument, and the use of a minor mode gives the genre its characteristic gravity. The genre has also become a stage show with modern arrangements, which is how many people now first encounter it, and that form keeps the call and response while adding orchestration. It is treated as part of the national cultural identity and is taught in schools, which is unusual for a folk genre and reflects how firmly it has been claimed as heritage.

entries.answer: Impressionism is a movement in painting from the late nineteenth century, and the name comes from a hostile review that mocked the loose visible brushwork, which is why the movement's own label is slightly an insult. The painters, Monet and Renoir among them, were working outdoors and painting quickly to catch the effect of a particular light at a particular moment, which is the real subject of the work. That is a genuine break from earlier painting, which was organised around subject matter and finished composition rather than about a view, and it is also why an impressionist picture of the same scene painted twice is two different pictures rather than a worse and a better version of one. The brushstroke is left visible, the edges are not always finished, and the colour is often mixed on the canvas rather than in precise amounts, which was a practical consequence of speed. The later development of post-impressionism is the term for the painters, including Van Gogh and Cezanne, who took the same approach and pushed it somewhere else.

patterns: how do i find out about an artist
entries.answer: An artist biography is the record of a career: where somebody trained, what they made, what changed and when. I can explain the subject and how the field is put together, and I can be accurate about work that is finished and settled, but I cannot tell you what a living artist released this month or what a current chart says. There is no live source behind this bank, so a name typed on its own is likely to be one I do not have, and I will say so rather than describe somebody's work I have not got.

entries.answer: An artist is somebody who makes work judged by something other than its function, and the word covers visual art, music, performance and writing without separating them cleanly. What unites the uses is that the making and the reception are the point, rather than a building being erected or a problem being solved. It is also a word that flatters, since calling something an art rather than a craft implies judgement that may not be there.

patterns: is oil paint better than acrylic
entries.answer: Painting is pigment applied to a surface, and the oldest surviving painted surfaces are cave walls thousands of years old, which shows the medium came first and the galleries came much later. Paint changes behaviour as it ages, which is why a painting is a record of materials as much as of decisions; oil keeps moving for centuries and continues to crack. Reproductions cannot fix that, since what is reproduced is an image rather than the substance, and that is the ongoing argument in museums.

entries.answer: A portrait is a representation of a person, and it is a negotiation rather than a record, since the sitter chooses how they are seen and the painter decides what to emphasise. A likeness and a good portrait are not the same goal: a likeness can be accurate and lifeless, and a good portrait tells you what the person is like. Photography changed the commercial half of the business almost completely, while the commissioned single portrait survives where status is the point.

entries.answer: The painters most often named are the ones whose work was reproduced enough to escape their own century, and that is a selection effect rather than a judgement of quality. The usual names cluster in a few periods because patrons funded them then, not because those centuries produced more talent. Most had ordinary lives and were unknown outside their city, and the canon was assembled much later by museums, dealers and textbooks.

patterns: is being a musician a good career
entries.answer: A musician is somebody who plays or composes, and the work splits into performance and composition in ways that used to be one job and now are rarely. The economics differ too, since performing income is unreliable and peaks early while composing income arrives late and can continue for decades. The shift that mattered in the last century was the recording, which separated the audience from the room and made it possible to be paid repeatedly for the same hour.

patterns: why do singers use stage names
is a stage name a pseudonym
entries.answer: A stage name is the name somebody performs under, and it is chosen far more often now than earlier performers could afford to do, when it was expensive to be a stranger. The reasons are now partly practical, since a name that is easy to say, spell and search changes how much money the work finds. It is also a signal that the person is being treated as a product, which is what a performer is both willing and ambivalent about.
